title: The Son Who Took His Share and Left
keyword: parable of the prodigal son explained
idea: The parable of the lost son (Luke 15:11-32) retold in plain words: a son takes his inheritance and wastes it, comes home with a speech, and a father runs to meet him; the elder brother stands outside

cast.name: Father
cast.look: old farmer, bald, white moustache, plain tunic

cast.name: Younger Son
cast.look: young man, short brown hair, blue shirt, a heavy coin bag

cast.name: Elder Son
cast.look: older brother, dark hair, green vest, work gloves

cast.name: Farmer
cast.look: stern pig farmer, bald, brown apron

scenes.title: The share
scenes.place: the family farm in the morning, a stone house, olive trees and a gate

lines.t: A son asked for his inheritance while his father was still alive.
The father loved them both. He had taught them to plow, to prune the olives, and to read the sky.
A man had two sons, and a farm that would one day be theirs.
The elder son did all of it well, and never asked for more than the work in front of him.
Father, give me my share now. I want to live my own life.
I do not want to wait thirty years for a farm. I want a life now.
Are you sure? A farm takes years to grow, and one winter to lose.
It was a hard thing to ask. It was like saying: I cannot wait for you to be gone.
He did not argue. He did not shout. He divided what he had.
The father looked at his son for a long time. Then he nodded.
A few days later the younger son packed his things, and left.

scenes.title: The far country
scenes.place: a loud city street at night, a crowded tavern with lanterns and a long table

lines.t: In the far country, nobody knew his name, and everybody liked his money.
He rented the biggest house on the street, and filled it with guests.
Another round for everyone! Tonight is on me!
He bought dinners. He bought gifts. He bought friends who stayed exactly as long as the coins did.
Stay as long as you like! There is always more where this came from.
He kept saying that. He did not look at the bag, which got lighter every week.
It felt like freedom. For a while, it even looked like freedom.

scenes.title: Empty
scenes.place: a bare street in the same city by day, an empty market and a closed tavern door

lines.t: The tavern door was locked. The big house had a new owner.
Then the coins ran out. And a famine came to the land.
I have nothing left. Where did my friends go?
I cannot even pay for a loaf of bread.
They had gone where the money was. That is the only place a friend like that can go.
He was hungry, and he did not know anyone, and there was no one to ask.
One morning he counted what he had left. It took no time at all.

scenes.title: The pigs
scenes.place: a muddy pig farm outside the city, a wooden fence, a trough and grey rain clouds

lines.t: I can use a hand. Feed the pigs. That is all I have.
No pay. You eat what the pigs leave.
For a young man from a good family, it was the lowest job there was.
He was so hungry that the pigs' food began to look good to him.
He thought about his father's farm. Even the hired workers there ate well.
My father's workers have bread to spare, and I am starving here.
And in that mud, something quiet happened. He stopped blaming everyone else.
I was a son in that house, and I threw it away for a few months of noise.
He did not make excuses to himself. For the first time, he told the truth.

scenes.title: The speech
scenes.place: a dusty country road in the late afternoon, a signpost and the farm far away on a hill

lines.t: He decided to go home. He did not expect to be a son again.
The road was long. His shoes were worn through, and his shirt was in rags.
Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. Make me one of your workers.
He practised it all the way. Every step, a little louder, a little more sure.
What if he does not even open the gate?
He did not know that someone had been watching that road every single day.

scenes.title: The run
scenes.place: the gate of the family farm at dusk, the dusty road and the father running toward it

lines.t: While he was still far off, his father saw him, and ran.
The father did not wait at the gate. He ran, and a man his age does not run.
My son! My son is home!
Father, I have sinned. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.
He hugged his son before the speech could start. The rags and the smell of the pigsty did not matter.
I was watching the road every day. I knew you would come.
Bring the best robe. Bring a ring, and sandals. Tonight we celebrate.
The speech he had practised never got finished. He did not need it.
The servants brought a robe, a ring, and sandals. Things that only a son wears.

scenes.title: The brother
scenes.place: a wheat field at sunset, the farm house with warm lights and a long table inside

lines.t: The elder son was in the fields. He came home to music and laughter.
What is all this noise? Whose party is this?
A servant told him: your brother is back, and your father has killed the fattened calf.
Years of work, and nobody ever killed a calf for me.
I never left. I worked every day. And I never got even a goat.
He stayed outside. He had every reason to be angry, and he was not wrong about the facts.
His father came out to him. He had run to meet one son. Now he walked out to meet the other.

scenes.title: Everything I have
scenes.place: the farm gate at night under lanterns, the father walking out to meet his elder son

lines.t: Son, you are always with me. Everything I have is yours.
He wasted everything, and you give him a feast?
But we had to celebrate. Your brother was lost, and now he is found.
He was lost, and now he is found. How could I not celebrate?
The story does not say whether the elder brother went inside.
Both brothers had been far from the father. One went to a far country.
The other was far away while standing right next to him.
It stops at the door, with the music behind it, and leaves that part to us.
Which brother are you tonight, and what would it take to walk in?
